status: Fixed in source (message seam); adjacent lane re-claim behaviour still open
area: Task claim ownership / lane session diagnostics
finding: ATM_TASK_CLAIM_OWNER_MISMATCH decided ownership on lane session ids but rendered its message from actor ids. compareClaimLifecycleOwners returns mode lane-id whenever both lifecycle records carry a lane id, and only falls back to actor ids when one is missing. throwIfClaimOwnerMismatch ignored that mode and always formatted "Task <id> is claimed by <currentActor>, not <requestedActor>". When one actor holds a task on an expired lane and re-claims from a freshly minted lane, both sides are the same actor, so the operator is told "Task TASK-PRF-0004 is claimed by claude-008, not claude-008" - a self-contradiction that points at an identity defect that does not exist. The correct recovery, laneAdoptCommand, was already present in the details payload but the prose actively argued against reading it. Setting ATM_LANE_SESSION_ID to the holding lane does not avoid the mismatch: the claim path still mints a new lane and compares against it, so explicit lane adopt is the only route.
expectedBehavior: The mismatch message must name whichever identity actually discriminated. In lane-id mode it must name the holding lane and the requested lane, and when both sides share one actor it must say so explicitly and point at lane adoption. In actor-fallback mode the existing actor wording is correct and must be preserved byte for byte. The machine-readable reason behind the verdict must also be exposed, not only the mode label.
evidenceOrRepro: Reproduced five times on 2026-08-25 across TASK-PRF-0002 and TASK-PRF-0004 during Product Proof parallel-claim runs: node atm.mjs next --claim --actor claude-008 --task TASK-PRF-0004 --auto-intent --json returned ATM_TASK_CLAIM_OWNER_MISMATCH with currentActor=claude-008, actorId=claude-008, ownershipMode=lane-id, holdingLaneSessionId=lane-20260825124249-claude-008-40b231e44e and requestedLaneSessionId=lane-20260825142953-claude-008-c593fc5a5b. Running the returned laneAdoptCommand and retrying once succeeded every time. Regression coverage added in tests/cli/claim-owner-mismatch-message.test.ts.
followUp: Two adjacent items stay open and were deliberately left out of this bounded message repair. First, tests/cli/tasks-claim-auto-intent.test.ts is red at HEAD independently of this change (verified by stashing the patch and re-running): a same-actor second claim on TASK-MAO-AUTO-0002 is rejected with ATM_LOCK_CONFLICT because two lanes were minted for actor captain. That is the same defect family one layer down - the lifecycle refuses a same-actor lane rotation instead of adopting or rotating it - and it needs its own card with authority over the claim path, not only its message. Second, next --task on an already-claimed task returns ATM_NEXT_TASK_SCOPE_NOT_FOUND because a held task is excluded from importedTaskQueue, and the official recovery chain next --task then next --prompt then guide loops back to orient with matchedIntent unknown; the only working route is the task-scoped claim command whose rejection carries laneAdoptCommand. Both should be triaged together with this row.
